tools.name: search
tools.description: Search bookable businesses on G-Guest by name or slug. Returns ids you can pass to fetch or to the booking tools.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Fetch full details for one business id returned by search: services, hours, timezone and how to book it.

tools.name: get_business
tools.description: Look up a business on G-Guest: services, opening hours, timezone and maximum party size. Call this first if you only know the slug.

tools.name: check_availability
tools.description: List bookable time slots for a business on a given date and party size. Offer the guest only slots where available is true.

tools.name: create_booking
tools.description: Create a real reservation. Use a start value returned by check_availability. Never invent guest details. Ask the person for their real name, email and phone first. If the result status is pending_confirmation, show the guest the confirmation_url.

tools.name: check_booking
tools.description: Look up one existing booking so the guest can confirm when and where it is. Identify it with the booking_id and manage_token that create_booking returned; both also sit in the guest's confirmation email as the manage link, /booking/<booking_id>?token=<manage_token>. findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "fetch" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "cancel_booking" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Cancel an upcoming booking and release its slot to other guests. Identified like check_booking: booking_id plus manage_token. Confirm with the guest before call…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_booking, request_listing · Private data: check_booking, request_listing · Public sink: create_booking, check_booking, request_listing.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_booking, request_listing · Private data: check_booking, request_listing · Public sink: create_booking, check_booking, request_listing

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
